Title: Asbestos fibres
Description: MLC also addresses occupational exposure to asbestos. If PSC finds flaking asbestos (e.g., around old pipe lagging), that’s a direct crew health hazard. They will detain until area is sealed or asbestos removed by professionals because crew inhaling fibers is unacceptab8】. Score 7.

Title: Preventative information
Description: Possibly ensuring safety and health information is posted (like posters on noise, etc.). Minor.

Title: Steam pipes, pressure pipes, wires (insulation)
Description: Duplicate of earlier 09211/09219 (insulation on hot pipes, proper cable insulation). Covered – high moderate for crew safety.
Mapped Questions-Internal: Airpipe coaming (save alls) & head in good conditon without heavy corrosion or holes.?
Mapped Questions-External: Is the pipe work in the machinery space, including but not limited to steam, fuel, lubricating oil, sewage, drain and air lines well maintained, in good condition and free of any temporary repair? (V)? # Are procedures in place to safeguard the ballast lines, hydraulic lines, fire lines and bunker lines in sub-freezing temperature? (V)?

Title: Access / structural features (ship)
Description: Duplicate of 09220 (safe structural design of work spaces), moderate.

Title: Exposure to harmful levels of ambient factors
Description: If crew are routinely exposed to harmful ambient factors like extremely high noise, extreme heat or cold beyond permissible levels without mitigation. PSC would rarely quantify this unless crew lodge complaint. If for example an engine room measured 100+ dB and crew had no ear protection (ties into PPE code), they’d cite it. Usually low by itself.

Title: Ship's occupational safety and health policies and programmes
Description: MLC mandates an OSH policy and possibly a safety committee. If none exists, it’s an ISM and MLC issue (company failure to address crew safety systematically). PSC will note it – moderate (lack of formal structure, though many safety elements covered by ISM anyway).
AMSA Trends: NCP 2024-25: Health and safety protection & accident prevention (MLC Title 4)
AMSA Recommendations: Develop and enforce occupational safety and health policies and programmes; conduct risk assessments and training; address unsafe practices and maintain records of incidents and corrective actions.
Mapped Questions-External: Are procedures in place for the control of hot work, are they incorporated in the safety management system and is there documented evidence of compliance?

Title: On board programme for the prevention of occupational injuries and diseases
Description: Similar to above – needing a proactive program (safety meetings, risk assessments). If absent, moderate ISM/MLC deficiency.
Mapped Questions-External: Has company provided training for on-board key personnel in recognising signs of mental health problems? (V)?

Title: Procedure for inspection, reporting and correcting unsafe conditions and for investigating and reporting on-board occupational accidents
Description: The ship should have a procedure for crew to report hazards, for someone to investigate accidents, and to implement corrective actions (basically ISM again). If PSC sees, say, accidents happened and nothing was learned or reported, they’ll cite this. It’s moderately severe as it leads to repeated accidents.
Mapped Questions-External: Does the master periodically review the effectiveness of the onboard Safety Management System, report the findings to shore based management and receive feedback from them? # Are there procedures for reporting, investigation and close-out of non-conformities, accidents, and hazardous situations available and are they being followed? (V)? # Are on-board safety meetings held regularly and, are they reviewed by the vessel’s manager and feedback provided where necessary? # Is there a complaints procedure on board and are seafarers aware of this procedure? (V)?

Title: Ship's safety committee
Description: If required (usually if >5 seafarers, MLC suggests a safety committee monthly), and none exists, PSC notes it. Minor to moderate – easily rectified by instituting meetings.
Mapped Questions-External: Are on-board safety meetings held regularly and, are they reviewed by the vessel’s manager and feedback provided where necessary?

Title: Investigation after accident
Description: Similar to 18429 but focusing on whether accidents are investigated. If a serious injury occurred and no investigation or preventive action was taken, PSC will issue this. It’s an ISM fail – moderate-high because not learning from accidents can lead to recurrence.
Mapped Questions-External: Are there procedures for reporting, investigation and close-out of non-conformities, accidents, and hazardous situations available and are they being followed? (V)?

Title: Risk evaluation, training and instruction to seafarers
Description: MLC requires that risks are evaluated and crew instructed in OSH matters. If PSC finds no evidence of risk assessments or safety training, it’s noted. This overlaps with ISM requirements of training and familiarization. Moderate.
AMSA Trends: Risk assessment and SMS compliance
AMSA Recommendations: Conduct comprehensive risk assessments for tasks such as working at heights or over the side; implement and enforce risk controls; ensure all crew follow and understand SMS procedureshttps://www.amsa.gov.au/news-community/news-and-media-releases/out-now-maritime-safety-awareness-bulletin-issue-21-managing#:~:text=Risk%20assessments%20are%20a%20criticalsafety%20tool
Mapped Questions-External: Has a safety officer been appointed and trained, and is the safety officer familiar with the principles and practice of risk assessment? (V)? # Are procedures in place for the control of hot work, are they incorporated in the safety management system and is there documented evidence of compliance? # Are the crew familiar with the helicopter operation at sea, and are records available to show that the proper communication, shipboard helicopter safety checklist and specific risk assessment conducted prior to helicopter operation? (V)? # Are cyber security policies and procedures being incorporated in the safety management system and was the cyber security management system evaluated and certified by Class? (V)?

Title: Other (Health protection, medical care...)
Description: Other MLC health items, e.g., maybe lack of sanitary food handling certificate for cook, or not providing mosquito nets in malaria areas, etc. Generally moderate default.
AMSA Trends: NCP 2024-25: Health and safety protection & accident prevention (MLC Title 4)
AMSA Recommendations: Take a proactive approach to health and safety protection; ensure compliance with MLC Title 4; respond to MLC complaints promptly and maintain a safe working environment.

Title: Other safety in general
Description: A safety deficiency that doesn’t fit any category above (rare, since the list is exhaustive).

Title: Other (SOLAS operational)
Description: Another catch-all, maybe for an operational issue not covered (like failure to carry out emergency steering drills could be here if not in other codes).

Title: Other (MARPOL operational)
Description: A catch-all for any MARPOL-related operational shortcoming not listed (maybe Ballast Water Management issues, though that’s its own convention and code not in this list). Could be used if, say, the ship’s Oil Record Book had unusual discrepancies not enough to call it clear pollution but concerning.
